I farm 14 mu here in Quzhou, and I've been doing wheat-maize rotation for 25 years now. My father did the same thing on this land before me. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the dealer tells me, but most of what I know comes from doing it year after year.

For my wheat this winter, I plant an improved variety — Jimai 22 has done well for me and for my neighbor Old Wang, so I stick with it. I use about 18 kg of urea per mu as base fertilizer, plus a bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15), about 40 kg per mu. That gives me roughly 24 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium as base. Then I topdress with another 10 kg of urea at jointing stage, so that's another 4.6 kg N. Total maybe 28-29 kg N per mu. I'd rather put on a bit extra than see the wheat turn yellow in April — a thin wheat field means a bad harvest, and that's a disaster for feeding 6 people. Wheat needs 3 irrigations from my well: one before winter, one at jointing, one at filling. Pesticide I spray twice — once for aphids and red spider, once mixed with the foliar fertilizer near flowering for scab. I use rotary tillage because the ground is already soft after maize and it saves diesel.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid right after wheat harvest in June — no-tillage direct seeding saves time because the rains come fast. I apply about 50 kg of compound fertilizer as base through the seeder, then topdress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage. That gives me roughly 17 kg N base plus 9 kg N topdress, about 26 kg N total. Maize here yields well — I expect around 600 kg per mu in a normal year. Two irrigations usually enough since summer has rain. I spray pesticide twice — once for armyworm when seedlings are young, once for borer at tasseling.

I budget carefully. Fertilizer alone costs me over 3000 yuan for the whole farm per season. I cannot afford to waste, but I also cannot afford a poor yield. I do what works.
